sentences.text: Fossils of Zhengheornis were uncovered during fieldwork in March to April 2024 near Yangyuan Village in Zhenghe County, Fujian Province, China.
The holotype—the specimen defining the species—is stored at the Institute of Vertebrate Paleontology and Paleoanthropology under accession IVPP V34168.
The vertebrae of its tail are reduced and shortened, indicating that tail shortening preceded the later fusion that produced the pygostyle in bird evolution.
Zhengheornis belongs to the early avialan lineage, with Z. buyu designated as the type species.
Phylogenetic studies position it within Avialae, branching after the families Anchiornithidae and the iconic Archaeopteryx but before the genus Baminornis.
Some analyses propose that Zhengheornis and Yuezhuornis together form a distinct sister clade named Zhengheornithidae.
It inhabited a swamp-like setting of the Nanyuan Formation in what is now China during the Late Jurassic Kimmeridgian to Tithonian ages, roughly 150 million years ago at the stage boundary.
The precise phylogenetic placement of Zhengheornis relative to Anchiornithidae, Archaeopteryx and Baminornis remains debated among researchers.
